extracted.intended_audience: hospital coders, Medicare payment analysts, health policy stakeholders, device/drug manufacturers, and other Medicare rule commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed modifications to the ICD-10 MS-DRG GROUPER logic for IPPS/LTCH PPS (FY 2027), including reassigning procedure codes, creating/deleting MS-DRGs, and the analytic criteria used to justify those changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of MS-DRGs (clinical coherence & resource use)
rubrics_metrics.description: The MS-DRGs are a classification system intended to group together diagnoses and procedures with similar clinical characteristics and utilization of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We generally seek to identify sufficient sets of claims data with demonstrated clinical similarity in developing diagnosis related groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical coherence in grouping
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed grouping changes should improve clinical coherence by grouping cases with similar clinical indications (for example, grouping pancreatic islet cell transplant procedure codes with pancreas transplant procedures because of similarity in clinical indication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While recognizing procedures are not exactly the same, procedures can be considered coherent given similarity in clinical indication; reassignment is supported when it makes MS-DRG assignments more clinically homogeneous and better reflect hospital resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of claims data to evaluate frequency and resource use
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine claims data (e.g., MedPAR file updates) to determine how often procedure codes are reported across MS-DRGs and to measure resource use (number of cases, average length of stay, average costs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulations of proposed GROUPER logic changes should be presented showing counts, average LOS, and average costs to support whether reassignments improve homogeneity and reflect resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-O.R. vs O.R. procedure designation affects assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure codes designated as non-O.R. procedures for purposes of MS-DRG assignment will not determine the surgical MS-DRG when an O.R. procedure is also reported; designation therefore affects which code governs grouping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ICD-10-PCS procedure codes describing introduction of pancreatic islet cells are designated as non-O.R. procedures affecting assignment only to MS-DRGs 673, 674, and 675; similarly, pafolacianine fluorescence-guided procedure codes are designated non-O.R. and thus the uterine/adnexa procedure code determines the surgical MS-DRG assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal diagnosis determines assignment when special diagnosis logic not present
rubrics_metrics.description: When diagnosis codes that trigger special MS-DRG logic (e.g., E10.21, E10.22, E10.29) are not reported as the principal diagnosis, the MS-DRG assignment is determined by the principal diagnosis and other procedures reported on the claim when specific procedure codes are assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated for pancreatic islet cell transplantation: if the special diabetes-with-kidney-complication diagnoses are not principal, other claim information governs assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of MS-DRGs should reflect assigned diagnoses/procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: MS-DRG titles should accurately reflect the diagnoses and procedures assigned to those groups, and titles may be revised to better reflect assigned procedures/diagnoses (e.g., adding 'Islet Cell' to pancreas-related DRG titles or revising 'Other' titles to reflect scope).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed title changes are intended to better reflect the assigned procedures effective the applicable FY date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary duplication in GROUPER logic (code clusters vs standalone codes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where procedure codes are already assigned as standalone procedures to an MS-DRG, including those same codes again within multi-code combinations (clusters) is redundant; GROUPER logic should avoid unnecessary duplicative code combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 0VT00ZZ and 0VT04ZZ (resection of prostate, open and percutaneous endoscopic approaches) are assigned to MS-DRGs 707/708 as standalone procedures; their inclusion within code clusters is therefore unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of procedure-specific codes with clinically appropriate MS-DRGs
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure codes should be assigned to the MS-DRGs that are most clinically aligned with the procedure described (e.g., transurethral prostatectomy codes align with MS-DRGs 713/714 rather than 707/708).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment decisions are informed by claim-level frequency, cost and LOS comparisons across candidate MS-DRGs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of statistical/quantitative metrics in simulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simulations to show the quantitative impact of proposed GROUPER changes on counts, average LOS, average costs, and cost variance for affected MS-DRGs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate whether adding logic lists has limited effect on average costs while improving clinical coherence; include tables for simulation results and reference GROUPER software versioning for public analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and exclusion logic to preserve intended groupings
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposing changes, add exclusion logic where necessary to maintain stability of related MS-DRGs (e.g., add logic to MS-DRG 010 to exclude cases also reporting kidney transplant procedures so those cases continue to group to MS-DRGs 008 and 019).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should consider downstream grouping stability and add explicit exclusions where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: When case counts are small, avoid premature subgrouping or reassignment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the number of cases reporting a procedure (or otherwise relevant observations) is very small, CMS may conclude it is premature to modify GROUPER logic or reassign cases for the upcoming FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small sample sizes and wide variance in costs/LOS undermine ability to ascribe resource use to a new technology; CMS will seek more claims data before acting (example: CYTALUX® cases were few and exhibited wide variance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other payment mechanisms for high-cost cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for statutory provisions that provide additional payments for extraordinarily high-cost cases (e.g., section 1886(d)(5)(A) of the Act) when evaluating whether MS-DRG reassignment is necessary to reflect incremental costs of an innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MS-DRG averages may mask outlier costs; NTAPs and extraordinary cost payments can be relevant to policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria to create severity-level subgroups (five established criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: All five criteria to create subgroups must be met for a base MS-DRG to be split by CC (severity level): (1) at least 500 cases in the MCC subgroup, the CC subgroup, and the without CC/MCC subgroup; (2) at least 5 percent of the cases are in each of the three subgroups; (3) at least a 20 percent difference in average costs between the MCC subgroup and the CC subgroup and between the CC group and NonCC subgroup; (4) at least a $2,000 difference in average costs between the MCC subgroup and the with CC subgroup and between the CC subgroup and NonCC subgroup; and (5) at least a 3-percent reduction in cost variance, indicating the severity-level splits increase the explanatory power of the base MS-DRG in capturing differences in expected cost by at least 3 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five criteria are applied (see section II.C.1.b.) to evaluate whether a three-way or other severity split is justified; example: proposed new uterine/adnexa malignancy MS-DRGs met the three-way split criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restructure MS-DRGs when resource utilization drivers change over time
rubrics_metrics.description: If analysis shows that resource utilization is now more related to procedures performed rather than diagnoses (or vice versa) compared to historic patterns, restructure MS-DRGs accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cited a 39-year historical change where uterine/adnexa resource use appears more related to procedures than to whether malignancy was ovarian/adnexal vs. non-ovarian/adnexal, supporting DRG restructuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document and publish logic lists, surgical hierarchy, and software for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide tables/lists of diagnosis and procedure codes used in proposed logic lists, reference surgical hierarchy discussions, and make a test version of the ICD-10 MS-DRG GROUPER software available to the public for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to tables (e.g., Table 6P.4a/b/c, Table 6P.5a/b) and section citations (e.g., II.C.14, II.C.1.b) guide stakeholders to the full documentation; note that test software may not yet reflect all proposed changes.
